content.title: Dennis Gates: 5 facts on the Mizzou basketball head coach
content.text: Head coach Dennis Gates of the Missouri Tigers looks on during the first half of a game against the Florida Gators at Stephen C. O'Connell Center on Jan. 14, 2025, in Gainesville, Florida.James Gilbert/Getty ImagesDennis Gates was announced as the University of Missouri men’s basketball head coach on March 22, 2022. He is the 20th head coach in the program's history. "We will build a program that all Mizzou fans will be proud of, for how we play, how our student-athletes represent the University of Missouri and how our togetherness and work ethic will lead to on-court victories,” Gates said in the statement announcing his hiring. Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢Mizzou went 25-10 overall and 11-7 in the SEC during Gates’ debut season. Mizzou finished fourth in the 2022-23 SEC standings, their highest finish in the conference at that point. Mizzou and Gates beat Utah State in the first round of the 2023 NCAA Tournament but got beaten by Princeton in the second round. Gates’ second season at Mizzou did not go so well. The Tigers finished 8-24 overall and 0-18 in the SEC. Here is some basic information about Mizzou basketball coach Dennis Gates: Height: 6 feet, 3 inches Age: 45 years old Birthday: Jan. 14, 1980 Hometown: Country Club Hills, Illinois High school: Whitney M. Young Magnet High School in Chicago College: California-Berkeley Wife: Jocelyn Gates Children: Avery, Duke and Denver Gates Article continues below this adFind out five more things to know about Missouri men’s basketball head coach Dennis Gates. What is Dennis Gates’ salary? Here are contract details Missouri Tigers head coach Dennis Gates answers questions in the postgame press conference following a first round game of the men's Southeastern Conference Tournament between the Missouri Tigers and the Georgia Bulldogs on March 13, 2024, at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee.Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire via Getty ImagesDennis Gates received a contract extension at the end of the 2022-23 season to keep him at Missouri through the 2028-29 season. Article continues below this adThe extension increased Gates’ salary to $4 million for the 2023-24 season with a $100,000 increase during each season of the contract, culminating with a salary of $4.5 million in 2028-29. Gates has bonuses in his contract that could add $655,000. "The city of Columbia is my home, my family loves it here and I wouldn't want to be anywhere else,” Gates said at the time of his contract extension. “My staff has done a tremendous job of supporting my dream building on the great tradition of Mizzou. I'm proud to be a Tiger and to coach at this wonderful institution."Gates’ salary during his first year at Missouri in 2022-23 was $2.5 million. Where did Dennis Gates go to college? He played basketball at CalDennis Gates #51 of the California Golden Bears reacts to a turnover against the Eastern Washington Eagles during the 1st Place Game of the BCA Classic at Haas Pavilion at the University of Berkeley, California in Berkeley, California, on Nov. 16, 2001.Donald Miralle/Getty ImagesDennis Gates played men’s basketball at Cal from 1998-2002, and he was a three-year captain. Ben Braun was the Bears’ head coach throughout Gates’ career. Article continues below this adCal won the 1999 NIT. Cal defeated Clemson 61-60 in the NIT championship game in Madison Square Garden. Cal also beat Fresno State, DePaul, Colorado State, and Oregon on the way to the 1999 NIT title. The Bears reached the NCAA Tournament in 2001 and 2002. Fresno State beat Cal 82-70 in the first round of the 2001 NCAA Tournament. No. 6-seeded Cal beat No. 11 seed Penn 82-75 in the first round of the 2002 NCAA Tournament, and Gates had six points off the bench. In the second round, No. 3-seeded Pitt coached by Ben Howland won 63-50 vs. Cal, and Gates had two points off the bench. For his Cal career, Gates appeared in 114 games and started 34 times. He averaged 3.8 points, 1.3 assists, and 1.2 rebounds in 13.8 minutes per game. Gates earned a bachelor’s degree in sociology from Cal. Article continues below this adDennis Gates guided Cleveland State basketball to the NCAA Tournament Head coach Dennis Gates of the Cleveland State Vikings celebrates with his team after winning the Horizon League tournament against the Oakland Golden Grizzlies at Indiana Farmers Coliseum on March 9, 2021, in Indianapolis, Indiana.Justin Casterline/Getty ImagesDennis Gates was the Cleveland State men’s basketball head coach from 2019-22. He guided the Vikings to Horizon League regular season championships in both 2020-21 and 2021-22. During the 2020-21 season, Cleveland State also won the Horizon League Tournament to capture an NCAA Tournament berth. CSU beat Oakland 80-69 in the Horizon League Tournament championship game. Article continues below this adNo. 15-seeded Cleveland State went against No. 2 seed Houston in the 2021 NCAA Tournament first round in Bloomington, Indiana. Coached by Kelvin Sampson, Houston beat CSU 87-56. Quentin Grimes led Houston with 18 points in the win. Houston reached the 2021 Final Four, where it lost to eventual national champion Baylor. Cleveland State’s only previous NCAA Tournament appearances came in 1986 and 2009. Gates earned Horizon League Coach of the Year honors in 2019-20 and 2020-21. Dennis Gates helped Florida State basketball reach 2018 Elite EightFlorida State assistant coach Dennis Gates talks to the team during the game at the Donald L. Tucker Center on Dec. 17, 2012, in Tallahassee, Florida.Jeff Gammons/Getty ImagesDennis Gates was a Florida State men’s basketball graduate assistant for the 2004-05 season, and he returned as an FSU assistant coach from 2011-19. Leonard Hamilton was the Florida State men’s basketball head coach throughout Gates’ time in Tallahassee. While Gates was on the FSU staff, Florida State made the NCAA Tournament in 2012, 2017, 2018, and 2019. Article continues below this adOf those four FSU teams, the 2018 team made the deepest NCAA Tournament run becoming just the third Florida State men’s basketball team to reach the Elite Eight – only previously done in 1972 and 1993. No. 9-seeded Florida State beat No. 8 seed Mizzou 67-54 in the first round of the 2018 NCAA Tournament in Nashville. That was followed by wins against No. 1 seed Xavier and No. 4 seed Gonzaga. No. 3-seeded Michigan coached by John Beilein ended the FSU run in Los Angeles. Dennis Gates was also a Marquette graduate assistant (2003-04), a Cal assistant coach (2005-07), a Northern Illinois assistant coach (2007-09), and a Nevada assistant coach (2009-11). Dennis Gates coached Keyon Dooling with ClippersKeyon Dooling #1 of the Los Angeles Clippers waits to enter the game against the Portland Trail Blazers at Staples Center on April 16, 2003, in Los Angeles, California. The Clippers won 107-93.Lisa Blumenfeld/Getty ImagesDennis Gates served as the skill development coach for the Los Angeles Clippers during the 2002-03 season right out of college. The Clippers went 27-55 overall that season. Article continues below this adAlvin Gentry was the Clippers head coach for the first 58 games, but after the team went 19-39 to start the season, interim coach Dennis Johnson replaced Gentry for the final 24 games. Former Missouri guard Keyon Dooling was a third-year NBA player on the 2002-03 Clippers. Dooling played 55 games and averaged 6.4 points, 1.6 assists, and 1.3 rebounds in 17.6 minutes per game that season. Dooling played in the NBA from 2000-13, and his longest stint was four years with the Clippers, who drafted him No. 10 overall in the 2000 NBA Draft. Dooling played at Mizzou from 1998-2000.
